Entertainment.title: Ralph Lauren Wins American Menswear Designer of the Year at 2026 CFDA Awards
Entertainment.text: SummaryRalph Lauren was named American Menswear Designer of the Year at the 2026 CFDA Fashion AwardsActor Matt Damon presented the award to Lauren who previously secured the menswear title in 1996 and 2007Lauren remains the only designer in history to claim all of the CFDA's top honors throughout his careerAmerican fashion institution Ralph Lauren took home the American Menswear Designer of the Year title at the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards, held Monday night at the American Museum of Natural History. The accolade marks the third time Lauren has secured the organization's highest menswear prize, following previous career wins in 1996 and 2007.Presented on stage by actor Matt Damon, Lauren topped an accomplished category of American designers that included Thom Browne, Todd Snyder, Willy Chavarria, and Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne of Public School New York. The achievement follows a monumental moment last year, when Lauren was named American Womenswear Designer of the Year for the second time following his initial win in 1995, underscoring his enduring influence across both sides of the industry.The triumph reinforces Lauren's unmatched legacy as the only designer in history to receive all of the CFDA’s top honors. His career recognitions span Lifetime Achievement, Menswear Designer of the Year, Womenswear Designer of the Year, and Retailer of the Year, in addition to prestigious tributes for Humanitarian Leadership, American Fashion Legend, and the organization's inaugural Popular Vote.The evening also spotlighted a distinguished lineup of fellow winners across the American and global fashion scene. Rachel Scott of Diotima captured the American Womenswear Designer of the Year prize, while high-jewelry sculptor Ana Khouri received American Accessories Designer of the Year. Elsewhere, Colleen Allen was honored with the American Emerging Designer of the Year award, and outgoing Yves Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello took home the International Designer of the Year Award. Entertainment.title: Crenshaw Skate Club Teams Up With Sprite for a Nostalgic Streetwear Capsule
Entertainment.text: SummaryCrenshaw Skate Club and Sprite debut a streetwear capsule blending skate and basketball cultures.Apparel includes tracksuits and graphic tees inspired by South Central LA barbershops.Releases November 7 in LA and November 9 online, priced 50–120.Crenshaw Skate Club is teaming up with Sprite on a collaborative capsule. Rooted in a shared appreciation for authenticity and cultural impact, the partnership merges Crenshaw Skate Club's distinct skate aesthetic with Sprite's historic ties to basketball and street culture. The lineup takes cues from Sprite's deep ties to basketball and street culture, spanning graphic T-shirts, sweatpants, a six-panel cap and an updated tracksuit, with an athletic mesh track jacket paired with oversized, baggy mesh shorts. Sprite's trademark green-and-yellow palette runs throughout, merging the visual identities of both brands.Much of the collection draws on founder Tobey McIntosh's own upbringing in South Central. One of the standout tees features an illustrated portrait with the Sprite logo cut into the subject's hair. The idea comes from the haircut menus McIntosh remembers seeing on barbershop walls when he went along with his father. Those charts offered patrons a range of designs to have shaved in, including well-known sports and pop culture logos. By turning that neighborhood fixture into a graphic, the design honors the small, everyday details that still shape Crenshaw Skate Club's point of view.The collection will debut at a special Los Angeles pop-up located at 439 N Fairfax Avenue, the original site of the Supreme store that became the first retailer to carry Crenshaw Skate Club's T-shirts in 2018. Returning to this exact location eight years later serves as a profound full-circle moment for the brand, honoring the spaces and community that fostered its early growth.The Crenshaw Skate Club x Sprite collection will be available exclusively at this Los Angeles pop-up on November 7, 2026, followed by a global online release on November 9, 2026, at 11 AM PST on the brand's website, with pieces ranging in price from $50 - $120 USD.Crenshaw Skate Club x Sprite Pop-Up439 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles,CA 90036, USAClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: H. Moser & Cie. Revisits Its Roots With Two New Heritage Collection Watches
Entertainment.text: SummaryH. Moser & Cie. adds two limited-edition steel watches to its pocket watch-inspired Heritage collection.The White fumé Chronograph revives a 1940s look with blue graphics and the 1947 logo.The Espresso fumé Centre Seconds adds oversized Globolight numerals.H. Moser & Cie. is revisiting its horological roots with two new additions to the vintage-inspired Heritage collection: the Heritage Chronograph White fumé and the Heritage Centre Seconds Espresso fumé. Heritage is the possibly the most understated line in the Maison's catalog, but also the one most closely tied to the history of a house founded in 1828. Its design language comes straight from the pocket watch era: round cases, slender tapered lugs from the period when pocket pieces were being adapted for the wrist, and a notched crown stamped with an "M." The new Heritage Chronograph White fumé and Heritage Centre Seconds Espresso fumé each draw on a different chapter of that history.The Heritage Chronograph White fumé takes its cues from Moser chronographs of the mid-20th century, when these instruments were made for explorers and adventurers who needed to time their journeys. The White fumé sunburst dial carries the brand's 1947 logo. The numerals, tachymeter scale, chronograph graduations and subdials are all printed in blue, a contrast that adds vintage charm and improves legibility. Subdials at 3 and 9 o'clock track the small seconds and a 45-minute chronograph counter, while sword-shaped hands and hour numerals are filled with Super-LumiNova. The 42 mm steel case is 13.8 mm thick and houses the automatic HMC 220 Manufacture caliber with a Dubois Dépraz chronograph module, which delivers a power reserve of at least three days. A grey kudu leather strap with matching grey hand-stitching completes the watch, and production is limited to 100 pieces at $34,100 USD.The Heritage Centre Seconds Espresso fumé recalls the early 20th century, when pocket watches were converted into wristwatches by adding slim lugs. It shares the 42 mm steel case, rounded profile and notched crown, but at 11.1 mm it sits noticeably slimmer on the wrist. The Espresso fumé sunburst dial adds warmth to the classic layout. A white railway minute track frames the edge, and oversized applied numerals in Globolight, a ceramic-based material containing Super-LumiNova, give the dial real presence alongside luminous sword-shaped hands. A logo in transparent lacquer keeps the branding subtle. The sapphire caseback shows the automatic HMC 200 calibre, finished with Moser double stripes and fitted with an original Straumann hairspring, which offers at least three days of power reserve. A brown kudu leather strap with white stitching completes the watch. It is limited to 200 pieces and priced at $18,300 USD.Visit H.
